source.title: Automatic Image-Level Morphological Trait Annotation for Organismal Images
source.authors: Vardaan Pahuja; Samuel Stevens; Alyson East; S. Record; Yu Su

record.tranche_reason: The study examines SAE feature semantics in vision-model representations and qualifies the idea that SAE features are canonical units: it gives examples of coherent localized features but notes that some latents may combine co-occurring traits and are not assumed to be the true underlying traits.
record.gate_note: The study does not test toy-model superposition, competition for dimensions, overlapping feature directions, or a sparsity-dependent geometric transition. Its SAE-sparsity ablations measure trait-description quality and coverage, not superposition geometry, so they are not rows for these claim versions. The neuron examples and the explicit qualification about mixed latents bear on V5.
record.test_reason: The paper uses ReLU SAEs on DINOv2 features as a tool for a trait-annotation pipeline. Its quantitative results (expert ratings, trait counts, BioCLIP zero-shot accuracy) measure the pipeline's own performance. It does not measure superposition, polysemanticity, or whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical. The neuron examples are a handful of hand-picked qualitative illustrations, and the 'mixed latents' remark is an untested caveat in the Limitations section. The subject is a vision backbone, not an LLM, so V4 as stated does not apply.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct but incomplete. The authors claim SAEs on foundation-model features yield monosemantic, spatially grounded part detectors. SAE-guided prompting raised expert ratings of trait descriptions (3.15 to 3.91, multi-image). Fine-tuning on the resulting BIOSCAN-Traits dataset improved BioCLIP zero-shot insect classification (34.8 to 39.9). In the Limitations section they hedge that latents may mix co-occurring traits and are not assumed to be the true traits.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ReLU SAEs on DINOv2-base vision features to identify localized morphological regions; does not reproduce Toy Models of Superposition or measure overlapping directions, feature capacity, or superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that SAE sparsity coefficient and normalized frequency threshold affect trait-description ratings and the number of retained traits; these are pipeline outcomes rather than tests of superposition geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: In a ReLU SAE (24,576 latents) trained on DINOv2-base features of insect images, several hand-picked top-activating latents localize to single body parts: wings, antennae, thorax, leg-body junction, eyes and abdomen. This evidence is qualitative only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs trained on vision-transformer features recover spatially localized, part-specific interpretable latents (a vision analogue of V4).

record.problems: For the claim-relevant feature-semantic evidence, the paper gives representative qualitative activation examples rather than systematic measurements of feature completeness, stability, or canonicality. The authors also note that ground-truth morphological trait annotations are absent and that some latents may combine co-occurring traits.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. The sparsity-coefficient and frequency-threshold ablations (Sections 4.3 and Appendix B, Tables 2–3 and B.2) report annotation quality or throughput, not feature overlap, canonicality, or superposition geometry.

untested.parts: No toy model, capacity test, interference geometry or sparsity-dependent transition.
No test of capacity competition or of important features getting dedicated dimensions.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
No LLM activations studied. Feature spread across neurons is not measured.
Completeness, stability across seeds or settings, and canonicality of SAE features are not measured. Only a few illustrative latents are shown.
Dimensionality of features is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader over-read the study as a V5 test. The monosemanticity claim in the abstract rests only on illustrative examples. The sparsity ablations measure annotation quality, not representation properties, and were correctly left out. Code: github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/sae-trait-annotation.

versions.untested_parts: No toy network, feature-over-dimension capacity test, overlapping directions, or sparsity-dependent geometric transition.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise from competition for limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test other causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The SAE is trained on DINOv2 vision features, not LLM activations; the study does not measure feature spread across neurons in LLMs.

Does not measure whether all SAE features are complete, stable across training runs or settings, or canonical units. It reports representative visual examples and explicitly allows some latents to combine co-occurring traits.
Uses individual SAE latent dimensions but does not test whether underlying features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.operation_detail: Inspected top-activating SAE latent units and their spatial activation patterns.
rows.measure: Qualitative anatomical localization and semantic coherence
rows.value: The text reports that neuron 4852 consistently activates on insect wings.
rows.note: A representative coherent feature is shown, but this does not establish that SAE features generally are complete, stable, canonical units.
rows.check: Hand-picked illustrative latent (wings). It has no baseline or systematic measure and does not assess completeness, stability or canonicality, so it does not bear on V5. It is a vision model, not an LLM, so it does not bear on V4.

rows.measure: Whether SAE latents correspond to single underlying traits
rows.value: The authors state that some latents might correspond to multiple co-occurring traits, giving “elongated + thin” as an example, and say they do not assume SAE features are the true underlying traits.
rows.note: This explicitly qualifies the claim that SAE features are complete, canonical units.
rows.check: This is not a result. It is a hedged caveat in the Limitations section ('some latents might correspond to multiple co-occurring traits') with no measurement behind it. It should not be a row, and 'partial' is unsupported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Representative SAE features and the authors' stated limitation
reader_labels.reason: Some shown units align with localized anatomical parts, but the authors note that latents can combine co-occurring traits and are not assumed to be true underlying units; the study does not establish completeness or stability. Rows r1–r7.
